title: Marketing Adventure 1: The 7 Ps
welcome_lead: Today you'll work the marketing mix — the seven Ps that turn a product into a sale.
meta_desc: Business Management Marketing: 7Ps mix — product, price, place, promotion, people, process, physical evidence.
final_note: You learned the seven Ps of the extended marketing mix and applied each.

walkthroughs.body_html:
McCarthy (1960) defined the 4 Ps.

Product — features, quality, brand.
Price — penetration, skim, cost-plus, premium, psychological.
Place — direct, retailer, wholesaler, online.
Promotion — above-the-line (ads), below-the-line (PR, sales promo).

Booms & Bitner (1981) added three Ps for services.

People — service staff are the product.
Process — the customer journey, queues, check-out.
Physical evidence — tangible cues (branded uniforms, fittings, packaging) that make services feel real.

The mix must be internally consistent.

A luxury product needs premium price, exclusive place, prestige promotion, well-trained people, smooth process and elegant physical evidence — Rolls-Royce, not a pop-up.

What is the difference between a stakeholder and a shareholder?
options: Stakeholders and shareholders are different spellings of the same word.
Just-in-time means finishing work right before the deadline.
A shareholder owns shares in the company; a stakeholder is anyone affected by or with interest in the business — employees, customers, suppliers, community, plus shareholders.
Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.

mcqs.q: How is Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) calculated?
options: ROCE is just net profit divided by revenue.
Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.
ROCE is the wages divided by hours worked.

Operating profit divided by capital employed (total equity + non-current liabilities), expressed as a percentage. It measures how efficiently the business uses its long-term financing to generate profit.
